title: Brindle and the Lost Shimmerwing
markdown:
High above the world, where waterfalls tumbled like silver ribbons and ravens croaked old secrets from rocky ledges, lived Witch Brindle. Her home was not a tall smoky tower. It was much cozier, tucked into the heart of the mountain: a snug cave smelling of dried herbs hanging in bunches, gentle potions bubbling softly. Always near was Lentil, her stoat: wild spirit in a twitching nose, heart as brave as a shiny new coin. Brindle was as sensible as a well-used broom and as delightfully odd as a frog wearing spectacles.

“Now, this is where it gets interesting.” A voice boomed, deep and bright, like a giant playing a harp, from everywhere at once. “For Brindle of the Crag and her loyal friend Lentil the Brave, a special adventure was about to begin.”

Brindle, polishing very shiny moss-green pebbles, did not even jump. She sighed, voice calm as a little stream. “Oh, Elwyn. Do you have to announce everything as if the whole world is watching? We’re just trying to have a quiet morning.”

Lentil perked his ears, tail giving a happy flick. “Adventure? That sounds wonderful. Maybe daring rescues and exciting escapes.”

The real problem was not the booming voice. Flicker was missing. Flicker was Brindle’s precious shimmerwing butterfly: pure magic, wings like a rainbow spun into silk, and a love of hide-and-seek. Today he had truly outdone himself. All that remained was a faint shimmer of magical dust on the workbench, like fallen starlight.

“He’s flown off again, hasn’t he?” A small thoughtful frown. She knew that sparkly dust. It always meant somewhere inconvenient.

“The wonderful Brindle faces her first challenge.” Elwyn again, this time from a big shiny raven on the windowsill, dark eye twinkling. “Her beloved Flicker, lost in the wild.”

“Flicker isn’t lost. He’s just misplaced. Lentil, fetch my satchel. Climbing ropes, a few of those very tasty honey cakes, and maybe some glow-worms, just in case.”

With a determined spark in her sensible grey eyes she stepped out of the herb-scented home. Lentil trotted beside her, little paws barely touching the ground. Green moss on ancient rocks. Waterfalls like silver ribbons. Steps carved long ago into mountain rock wound upward into misty clouds. Ravens watched them go with knowing eyes.

“Get ready,” Elwyn announced, now the wind through the passes. “This part is where our heroes go down into the quiet Gorge of Whispers.”

The gorge was truly amazing. Rock walls dropped into a dark echoing canyon. Far below a river roared like a hidden giant. A bridge of woven vines stretched across the dizzying gap. Brindle, looking closely, saw it was surprisingly strong, even if a little wobbly.

“Hold on tight.” Lentil was already halfway across, brave spirit unbothered by the drop.

Brindle, ever practical, tested each step, quiet precision. Halfway she stopped. Not scared. Curious. The air felt cooler. A soft magical glow came from beneath the bridge, where the canyon was deepest. “Ah. Glow-worms. They always choose the most beautiful hidden places.” Hundreds of tiny green lights pulsed in the darkness, a scattered constellation among the river stones. A secret the earth shared.

“A test of bravery,” Elwyn boomed, perhaps a bit too loudly. “The brave Brindle must face her fears.”

“My only fear, Elwyn, is running out of good tea before it’s time for a cuppa.”

They reached the other side, a small hidden alcove in the cliff, a secret garden. There, on a patch of glowing purple mushrooms, sat Flicker, wings pulsing with soft beautiful light. He had not just picked a pretty spot. He had landed on a very strange, very small, carefully carved wooden music box.

“You see?” Brindle explained to Lentil, as if this were perfectly normal for a butterfly. “Flicker loves music. This music box plays the loveliest tinkling tune. It must have fallen from a traveller’s pack a long time ago. Flicker probably found it and wanted to keep it safe, or maybe just enjoy the music.” She picked it up and gently wound it. A sweet delicate melody filled the air.

“Aha.” Elwyn sounded almost happy, as if he had planned it. “The very creature Brindle was looking for has shown its own amazing purpose.”

Brindle scooped Flicker onto her finger. The butterfly’s light grew softer. He nuzzled a silent thank you. Lentil sniffed the music box. “It smells like old adventures and forgotten songs.”

She carefully closed it. The melody stopped. “Perhaps some creatures just like a good song and a safe quiet place to listen. You know, Elwyn, if you are going to be so mysterious and dramatic, you could at least be on time with your announcements.”

Elwyn chuckled like tiny bells. They started the walk back, Flicker fluttering around Brindle’s head like a living jewel, Lentil trotting faithfully beside her. The elf musician began a new song: not battles or monsters, but cozy homes, good friends, and the quiet happy feeling of finding what you have lost, even when it was exactly where it wanted to be. The setting sun painted pink and gold. Brindle felt a warmth as comforting as a perfectly brewed cup of her favourite herbal tea.
characters: Brindle (sensible mountain witch), Lentil (a stoat with a twitching nose)
audience: children aged 9-10, amusing fantasy story for middle-grade readers
author: StoryGen Community
